t: You're looking at the Royal Air Force Memorial on the Victoria Embankment. It was unveiled in 1923 to remember the Royal Air Force's casualties of the First World War, and by extension those of every conflict since. It is regarded as the official memorial of the RAF and related services, and it is listed Grade II star. Two men made it: the architect Sir Reginald Blomfield, and the Scottish sculptor Sir William Reid Dick, who later served as Sculptor in Ordinary for Scotland to two monarchs.
